jq is part of 3 of my public repositories, from 2014 to 2026.

What it was for: [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (1), [Security and OSINT](@/projects/security.md) (1) and [Systems and infrastructure](@/projects/systems.md) (1).

Most recently: [osint-case-ratcliffe-moscow-2026](@/work/osint-case-ratcliffe-moscow-2026.md): Open-source intelligence assessment of the CIA Director's unannounced Moscow visit (2026-08-25) — maintained with Claude Code skills; reusable OSINT case toolkit; [docker-datasciencetoolbox](@/work/docker-datasciencetoolbox.md): Dockerized http://datasciencetoolbox.org; [apollo-box](@/work/apollo-box.md): All needed data science stuff in one box.

1 of these projects runs as a live site.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses jq: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links jq to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
